standards.name: Core Scientific Dataset Model (CSDM)
standards.abstract: The Core Scientific Dataset (CSD) model describes a lightweight, portable, JSON-serializable representation for multi-dimensional scientific datasets: p-component dependent variables discretely sampled at M points in a d-dimensional coordinate space. It targets datasets from spectroscopy, diffraction, imaging and other disciplines that can be represented on orthogonal (regular or rectilinear) grids, and it is intentionally minimal — it encapsulates data values and the minimum metadata needed to represent them in an appropriate coordinate system. The model and its reference implementation (the Python csdmpy package) were published and described in Srivastava et al., PLOS ONE (2020) to address the lack of a portable, vendor-independent format for multi-dimensional scientific data and to enable easy import/export and processing with NumPy-compatible tools.

classification.rationale: The source presents explicit, field-level structure: class-attribute tables and enumerations (e.g. "Table 1 The description of the attributes from the Dimension class...", enumerations for QuantityType/NumericType/EncodingType, and a JSON-mapping table). These are concrete named attributes with defined types/encodings (not just a prose checklist), so the material is best represented as a MetadataTable.

CSDM.description.name: description
CSDM.description.descr: Brief human-readable description of the dataset contents (optional root-level attribute).
CSDM.description.evidence: At the root level, the CSDM object includes various useful optional attributes that may contain additional information about the dataset. One such useful attribute is the description key, which briefs the end-users on the contents of the dataset.

raw_full_info.quote: At the root level, the CSDM object includes various useful optional attributes that may contain additional information about the dataset. One such useful attribute is the description key, which briefs the end-users on the contents of the dataset.

CSDM.filename.name: filename
CSDM.filename.descr: Filename associated with the CSDM object/file.

CSDM.version.name: version
CSDM.version.descr: CSDM format or file version identifier.

CSDM.dimensions.name: dimensions
CSDM.dimensions.descr: List of Dimension objects defining the d-dimensional coordinate grid.
CSDM.dimensions.evidence: In csdmpy, dimensions and dependent variables are structured as list object. To access these lists, use the dimensions and dependent_variables attribute of the CSDM object, respectively.

raw_full_info.quote: In csdmpy, dimensions and dependent variables are structured as list object. To access these lists, use the dimensions and dependent_variables attribute of the CSDM object, respectively.

CSDM.dependent_variables.name: dependent_variables
CSDM.dependent_variables.descr: List of DependentVariable objects; each holds one or more components sampled on the coordinate grid.
CSDM.dependent_variables.evidence: An instance of the CSDM object may include multiple dimensions and dependent variables. Collectively, the dimensions form a multi-dimensional grid system, and the dependent variables populate this grid.

raw_full_info.quote: An instance of the CSDM object may include multiple dimensions and dependent variables. Collectively, the dimensions form a multi-dimensional grid system, and the dependent variables populate this grid.

Dimension.coordinates.name: coordinates
Dimension.coordinates.descr: Coordinate values along a dimension; represented as an Astropy Quantity whose .value is a NumPy array (numeric coordinates with units).
Dimension.coordinates.evidence: Note x[0].coordinates returns a Quantity instance from the Astropy package. In the csdmpy module, the Quantity.value is a Numpy array.

raw_full_info.quote: Note x[0].coordinates returns a Quantity instance from the Astropy package. ... In the csdmpy module, the Quantity.value is a Numpy array.

Dimension.description.name: description
Dimension.description.descr: Optional human-readable description for a Dimension object.
Dimension.description.evidence: Every instance of the Dimension object has its own set of attributes that further describe the respective dimension. For example, a Dimension object may have an optional description attribute, >>> x[0].description 'A temporal dimension.'

raw_full_info.quote: Every instance of the Dimension object has its own set of attributes that further describe the respective dimension. For example, a Dimension object may have an optional description attribute, >>> x[0].description 'A temporal dimension.'

DependentVariable.components.name: components
DependentVariable.components.descr: The sampled data values (one or more components). Stored in memory as a NumPy array with shape (p, N0, N1, ...), where p is the number of components and Ni are points along each dimension.
DependentVariable.components.evidence: Every dependent variable object has at least one component. ... The components attribute is a Numpy array. Note, the number of dimensions of this array is d+1, where d is the number of Dimension objects from the dimensions attribute.

raw_full_info.quote: Every dependent variable object has at least one component. ... The components attribute is a Numpy array. Note, the number of dimensions of this array is d+1, where d is the number of Dimension objects from the dimensions attribute.

DependentVariable.encoding.name: encoding
DependentVariable.encoding.descr: Serialization encoding for the dependent-variable data when writing CSD files.
DependentVariable.encoding.evidence: There are three encoding types for the dependent variables: none base64 raw. By default, all instances of DependentVariable from a CSDM object are serialized as base64 strings.

raw_full_info.quote: There are three encoding types for the dependent variables: none base64 raw. Note By default, all instances of DependentVariable from a CSDM object are serialized as base64 strings.

DependentVariable.unit.name: unit
DependentVariable.unit.descr: Unit of the dependent variable components (handled via astropy.units Quantity objects).
DependentVariable.unit.evidence: The csdmpy module utilizes the units library from astropy.units module to handle physical quantities. The numerical value and the unit of the physical quantities are accessed through the Quantity instance, using the value and the unit attributes, respectively.

raw_full_info.quote: The csdmpy module utilizes the units library from astropy.units module to handle physical quantities. The numerical value and the unit of the physical quantities are accessed through the Quantity instance, using the value and the unit attributes, respectively.

standards.notes: This extraction focuses on the concrete, field-level parts of the CSDM specification as presented in the PLOS ONE article and the csdmpy documentation (class-attribute tables and enumerations). The original paper also contains UML class diagrams and multiple enumeration tables (QuantityType, NumericType, EncodingType) and JSON-mapping guidance (Table 6) that can be added here as additional fields if you want a more exhaustive machine schema.
